2.text: Local Russian tradition states that part of the Cossacks, annoyed at the

3.text: hardships of an aimless and endless campaign, left Pavlutsky and returned to

4.text: the Kolyma. As the leader of this act, the name of Krivogornizyn is mentioned,

5.text: who was pyatidesyatnik (literally, “chief of fifty men,” the second degree of

6.text: commissioned officer in the Cossack regiment). During the time of my

7.text: travels, a man of that name still lived on the Lower Kolyma, in the village

8.text: of Pokhotsk, which is the centre of the ancient Cossack population. He was

9.text: reputed to be a descendant of the “traitor.” He was quite blind and extremely

10.text: poor. The people said that he was being punished for the sins of his ancestor.

14.text: He wanted to exterminate the whole Chukchee people. When murdering

15.text: people, he would gather up the fur caps of the killed men. Twenty sledges

16.text: loaded with caps he sent to the Sun Chief (the Emperor). He said, “No

17.text: more are left. I exterminated them all.” The Sun Chief answered, “There

18.text: are still numerous little birds hidden in the grass.” — “Then I will go and

19.text: finish them.” Therefore, when he is defeated and taken prisoner, the Chuk-

20.text: chee, in their turn, torture him and put him to a cruel death. Russian and

21.text: Tungus tradition also mentions that Pavlutsky was taken prisoner and tortured

22.text: to death. He was wounded and fell to the ground; but the Chukchee for a

23.text: long time could find no place in his armor through which to deal a mortal

24.text: blow. Only when the armor was untied and opened, was be stabbed in the
24.note: Printed 'was be stabbed' — the book's own error ('be' for 'he'); keyed verbatim per keying_spec.md §2.14 ("A printer's error is keyed as printed"). class: print.

25.text: neck. Chukchee tradition says that he was wounded in the right eye, then

26.text: killed with a knife thrust into the abdomen under a joint of the armor.

27.text: Another version says that he was stripped of armor and slowly roasted over

28.text: a big fire, and that the roasted meat was cut off piece by piece and thrown

29.text: away. Still another version mentions that he was stripped naked and made

30.text: to run around on the snow, being urged on like a young reindeer with a

31.text: heavy wooden club tied to his head.¹ All this time he was beaten with whips

32.text: and tent-dusters, and every blow drew blood. So he died.

33.text: A very interesting tale collected on the middle course of the Anadyr

35.text: against the Russians. Manaˊqtun was taken captive. Maˊnê, in his turn,

36.text: captured single-handed a Russian ship on which a great commander was

37.text: travelling up the river. This was done in the following manner. At some

38.text: rapids several Cossacks were walking along the shore, towing the ship. Maˊnê

39.text: concealed himself among the bushes and awaited their approach. They were

40.text: making great efforts, because the ship was very heavy, and they were unarmed.
